video_caption: The video opens with a split screen displaying two images of protests. On the left, a person of color in a white shirt carries a large sign that reads, "STOP MAKING PROFIT OUT OF PEOPLE'S LIVES" (along with a ribbon and heart symbol at the bottom), with a crowd blurred in the background. On the right, a street protest shows people holding signs; one in the foreground partially reads, "8,500 AIDS DEATHS DAILY...", while another in the background states, "AIDS DRUGS FOR EVERY NATION!". The scene then shifts to a white background with text in black, highlighting "schoolyard rumors" in red, describing HIV and AIDS as a "hot topic" in 1980s media. Below this text, four vintage public awareness posters are displayed: one depicting a glass with dark liquid and the text "Some people think you can catch AIDS from a glass. You can't."; another shows a person on a toilet seat with the text "CAN YOU GET AIDS FROM A TOILET SEAT? NO."; a third features a man holding a chalice with text questioning, "IS IT SAFE? THE CHALICE AND AIDS..."; and the fourth is a child's drawing of a stick figure with a red heart, saying, "I HAVE AIDS Please hug me I can't make you sick". The video then presents a two-part timeline of the AIDS epidemic, covering events from 1987 to 1989 and 1990 to 1995, detailing key developments in research, awareness, policy, and public figures. Finally, the scene transitions to a complex scientific diagram illustrating the genetic makeup of various lentiviruses: EIAV (Equine Infectious Anemia Virus) associated with a horse, FIV (Feline Immunodeficiency Virus), BIV (Bovine Immunodeficiency Virus), and OMVV (Ovine Maedi-Visna Virus) linked to a cat, cow, and sheep respectively. HIV-1's genetic structure is also shown below these, with lines connecting the cow and sheep images to the HIV-1 diagram, suggesting a potential origin. In the bottom center, a person (possibly male) wearing black VR-like glasses is shown getting blood drawn from their arm by a person in a blue glove, while medical supplies are visible on the table. To the bottom right, a detailed scientific illustration of an HIV virion, showing its internal and external components, is displayed.

The video segment features a static image divided into several sections, primarily illustrating different lentiviruses and their hosts, along with genetic and structural representations. On the top left, a brown horse is shown next to the text "EIAV" (Equine Infectious Anemia Virus), which is linked to a genetic diagram of the EIAV genome. Below the horse, images of a cat, a cow, and a sheep are displayed, next to the text "FIV/BIV/OMVV" (Feline Immunodeficiency Virus / Bovine Immunodeficiency Virus / Ovine Maedi-Visna Virus), also linked to their respective genetic diagrams. At the bottom left, a person's arm is seen receiving an injection from an unseen individual, with medical supplies on a table in the background. This image is associated with "HIV-1" (Human Immunodeficiency Virus type 1), which has its own genetic diagram below the others. The genetic diagrams label various genes and proteins, such as "gag," "pol," "tat," "rev," and "env," with specific components like "dUTPase" and "RNAseH" highlighted in red boxes. On the bottom right, an illustrative cross-section of a virus particle, likely HIV, shows its internal structure, including RNA, enzymes, capsid, and envelope components. The narrator mentions that these viruses "pursue similar, if slightly different life cycles" and infect "CD4 positive T cells and macrophages."

The video opens with a screen displaying a large block of genetic sequence text. At the top, the text reads ">gil 1906382|gb|K03455.1|HIVHXB2CG Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HXB2), complete genome; HIV1/HTLV-III/LAV reference genome" (This identifies the shown sequence as the complete genome of HIV-1 type 1, strain HXB2). Below this, numerous lines of the letters A, C, G, T, represent the DNA sequence itself. This text then transitions to a phylogenetic tree diagram which illustrates the evolutionary relationships between different strains of HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) and SIV (Simian Immunodeficiency Virus) and their animal hosts. The diagram is primarily black and white with red outlines highlighting the two main human virus types. On the left, a red outline encircles the "HIV-1" group, which is further divided into "HIV-1 group O", "HIV-1 group N", and "HIV-1 group M" (containing sub-branches labeled A through K). Several SIV strains from chimpanzees, such as "SIVcpzANT", "SIVcpzGAB", and "SIVcpzUS", are shown to be closely related to these HIV-1 groups. On the right, another red outline encompasses the "HIV-2" group, including "HIV-2 subtype B" and "HIV-2 subtype A". These HIV-2 strains are linked to various SIV strains found in macaques, mangabeys, and African Green Monkeys, such as "SIVmac239", "SIVsm", "SIVtan1", and "SIVveragrn", among others. The branches of the tree visually represent the genetic distance and evolutionary divergence between these viruses.

The video segment opens with a world map depicting the global distribution of HIV subtypes, accompanied by pie charts for different continents and a larger global total chart showing percentages for Subtype B (47.2%), Subtype C (26.7%), Subtype A (12.3%), Subtype D (5.3%), CRF_AE (3.2%), and Others (5.3%). Below the map, text in a green box reads, "Group M, Subtype B dominates the "West", Subtype C dominates Africa and Asia, and A dominates Central Europe and Russia." (Group M, Subtype B dominates the "West", Subtype C dominates Africa and Asia, and A dominates Central Europe and Russia.) To the right, a hierarchical diagram illustrates the classification of HIV-1 and HIV-2, with HIV-1 Group M branching into various subtypes (A, B, C, D, F, G, H, J, K, CRFs), and Subtype B highlighted. The video then transitions to a table detailing the "Estimated per act risk for acquisition of HIV by exposure route" (Estimated per act risk for acquisition of HIV by exposure route), listing various routes like blood transfusion (9,000 estimated infections per 10,000 exposures), childbirth (2,500), needle sharing (67), and different types of sexual intercourse, including receptive anal (50) and receptive oral (1). Adjacent to the table, red text emphasizes that "High risk activities involve exchange of large amounts of blood product in a protected environment. Transfusion, childbirth, sharing needles." (High risk activities involve exchange of large amounts of blood product in a protected environment. Transfusion, childbirth, sharing needles.)

The video segment displays a static image on a white background, featuring a table on the left and text on the right. The table, titled "Estimated per act risk for acquisition of HIV by exposure route [1]", lists various exposure routes and their estimated infections per 10,000 exposures to an infected source. Routes include "Blood Transfusion" (9,000), "Childbirth" (2,500), "Needle sharing injection drug use" (67), "Percutaneous needle stick" (30), "Receptive anal intercourse*" (50), "Insertive anal intercourse*" (6.5), "Receptive penile-vaginal intercourse*" (10), "Insertive penile-vaginal intercourse*" (5), "Receptive oral intercourse %" (1), and "Insertive oral intercourse %" (0.5). To the right of the table, bolded text in red highlights, "High risk activities involve **exchange of large amounts of blood product** in a protected environment. Transfusion, childbirth, sharing needles."

The video segment presents two slides illustrating the origin and early spread of a virus, likely HIV. The first slide shows a map of Central Africa with text overlay: "infected chimps in red circle" and "bushmeat hunters followed river south." A red dashed circle highlights an area encompassing parts of Cameroon, Central African Republic, and the Republic of the Congo. A red line traces a path from this circle, following what appears to be the Sangha and Congo rivers, south to Kinshasa (labeled Leopoldville). To the right, two black and white photographs depict "Leopoldville, 1896," showing an undeveloped, sparse settlement, and "Leopoldville, 1955," revealing a bustling urban center with cars and buildings. The second slide displays scientific data, including a diagram of "HXB2 sites" showing genetic segments (gag, pol, env), a phylogenetic tree representing "35 subtype A/A1 sequences" with branches indicating evolutionary relationships and dates (e.g., 1960, 1997), and a histogram comparing "Within subtype" and "Between subtype" uncorrected pairwise distances. Accompanying text on the right states: "A phylogenetic analysis of samples from African patients in 1959-1960 show several HIV positive, and the arrangements of mutations show that the infection was already widespread and diverse in sequence. This supports a viral host species transfer around 1931. Nature 455, 661-664 (2 October 2008)." The segment suggests that a transfer of the virus from chimpanzees to humans occurred around 1931, and its spread was facilitated by factors such as bushmeat hunting and the growth of urban centers like Leopoldville.

The video opens with a map of Central Africa, highlighting an area in Cameroon and the Central African Republic with a red circle, marked "infected chimps in red circle." A red line traces a path from this circle down the Congo River to Kinshasa (then Leopoldville), captioned "bushmeat hunters followed river south." Adjacent to the map are two sepia-toned photographs: "Leopoldville, 1896" shows a wide, undeveloped landscape, while "Leopoldville, 1955" depicts a bustling city street with cars and buildings. The scene transitions to a line graph tracking population growth for several African cities (Kinshasa, Brazzaville, Yaoundé, Bangui, Libreville, Douala) from 1880 to 1970, showing a significant increase after 1910. Text states, "In the countries surrounding the putative zone of cross-species transmission (current-day Cameroon, Central African Republic, DRC, Republic of Congo, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea) there was not a single site with a population exceeding 10,000 until after 1910," referencing "Nature 455, 661-664 (2 October 2008)." Following this, four more black and white photos illustrate Leopoldville's development: "1898, Leopoldville" shows a steam train with a crowd and a rural landscape; "1950, Leopoldville" displays a long bus, a busy street with palm trees, and a woman in front of a "NIGHT CLUB ORCHESTRA" sign. A map of Africa from 1914, colored by colonial occupation, appears next, with a red circle indicating the HIV origin area. Overlaid text reads, "It could be said that it was not African culture that led to the spread of HIV, but the effect of colonialism and industrialization in an area that has frequent contact with our close primate relatives." The video then shows a population density map of Africa, again with a red line tracking the spread from the origin, explaining, "Previous zoonotic transfers of HIV...were previously isolated by the low infection rate for anything but blood-blood contact. It was the addition of injectable drugs, prostitution, and urbanization that probably allowed HIV to escape the small region in which it frequently emerged." The narrative concludes with a world map showing a red line from Africa to Haiti and then to the US, with an inset map of the Caribbean, stating, "It appears that the next link in the chain was either to Haiti by direct immigration or directly to the US, or it might have been spread to Europe by sailors on cargo ships and then to North America." The final image is a world map depicting HIV-1 subtype distribution, along with a diagram classifying HIV types, noting, "Group M, Subtype B dominates the 'West', Subtype C dominates Africa and Asia, and A dominates Central Europe and Russia."

The video segment opens with a world map displaying pie charts indicating the global distribution of HIV-1 subtypes. A large pie chart in the bottom-left corner, labeled "Global Total," details the percentages of various subtypes, with Subtype B dominating at 47.2% and Subtype C at 26.7%. Smaller pie charts are overlaid on specific continents, showing regional subtype prevalence. Simultaneously, a hierarchical diagram on the bottom right illustrates the classification of HIV-1 into groups (M, N, O, P) and Group M into subtypes (A, B, C, D, F, G, H, J, K, CRFs), with Subtype B highlighted. Overlaying text states, "Group M, Subtype B dominates the "West", Subtype C dominates Africa and Asia, and A dominates Central Europe and Russia." The scene then transitions to a black and white image of a man with blonde hair and a mustache, with the text "PATIENT ZERO" and "THE MAN WHO BROUGHT THE AIDS EPIDEMIC TO CALIFORNIA" below him. A silhouette of a man carrying a briefcase walks above him. On the right, a diagram illustrates a disease transmission chain, starting with a "primary case (patient zero)" at the apex and branching down to numerous individuals, some highlighted in red to denote infection. The final scene presents a collage of images related to AIDS origin theories: a book cover titled "THE RIVER A JOURNEY TO THE SOURCE OF HIV AND AIDS" by Edward Hooper, a partial screenshot of a website "Origin of AIDS.com" with a featured article "Early Hepatitis B Vaccines and the 'Man-Made' Origin of HIV/AIDS," and another partial screen displaying "OPV-HIV" with associated "Hazard" and "Casualties" statistics, along with fragmented text discussing a "hypothesis" and "oral polio virus."

The video segment features a collage of images related to the origins of AIDS. On the left, the cover of a book titled "THE RIVER" by Edward Hooper is displayed, showing a landscape with a winding road or river. In the center, a webpage from "Origin of AIDS.com" is visible, featuring an article titled "Early Hepatitis B Vaccines and the 'Man-Made Origin of HIV/AIDS'" (meaning: discussing a theory about the artificial origin of HIV/AIDS related to early Hepatitis B vaccines), with additional text beginning, "This article regards a matter of global urgency...". On the right, a red graphic with "OPV-HIV" (referring to Oral Polio Vaccine and HIV) is shown, alongside a table listing "Hazard(0-1000)" and "Casualties" with numerical values, and partial text mentioning "hypothesis, result of the with an oral teen cultured the transfer ciency virus." A male narrator explains that Edward Hooper's book suggests an SIV-contaminated chimpanzee culture was used for the oral polio vaccine in the late 1950s and early 1960s. The scene then transitions to display two more book covers. On the left is "AIDS AND THE DOCTORS OF DEATH - AN INQUIRY INTO THE ORIGIN OF THE AIDS EPIDEMIC" by Alan Cantwell Jr., M.D., featuring a syringe on the cover. On the right, a book titled "The Man Made Plaques" by Mike Treis has a cover with red, blood-like dripping letters, a hand holding a syringe over a crest, and silhouettes of gravestones at the bottom. A red box highlights the "q" in "Plaques," and text bubbles ask "??? Plaques?" (meaning: questioning the nature or existence of "plaques"). The narrator states that this theory, effective for selling books and appealing to conspiracy theorists, proposes the SIV-contaminated vaccine culture as the origin of AIDS.

The video begins with a slide displaying three scientific graphs and descriptive text (0:03-0:06). Graph 'a' shows a genomic map of HXB2 sites, indicating genes like 'gag', 'pol', and 'env'. Graph 'b' presents a phylogenetic tree illustrating 35 subtype A/A1 sequences with dates from 1960 to 2002 and a scale of "0.07 substitutions per site". Graph 'c' is a frequency distribution plot, "ZR59 versus DRC60: 11.7%", with two peaks, "Within subtype" (purple) and "Between subtype" (orange), showing "Uncorrected pairwise distances". The accompanying text reads: "A phylogenetic analysis of samples from African patients in 1959-1960 show several HIV positive, and the arrangements of mutations show that the infection was already widespread and diverse in sequence. This supports a viral host species transfer around 1931. Nature 455, 661-664 (2 October 2008)". The scene then transitions to a table titled "Table 1 Oral poliovirus vaccine samples tested" (0:06-0:16). This table lists various Wistar and CDC polio vaccine samples, indicating whether they tested positive (+) or negative (-) for "SIVcpz/HIV-1" and "Polio". All samples tested negative for SIVcpz/HIV-1 and positive for Polio. Below the table, there's a detailed explanation about the testing methodology and controls, with a citation "Nature 410, 1045-1046 (26 April 2001)". Next, three black and white historical photographs appear (0:16-0:30): one on the left shows a man in a shirt and tie operating a large piece of laboratory equipment; a middle image depicts a person looking intently through a microscope; and a smaller image on the top right shows two men in lab coats working at a laboratory bench with bottles on shelves. The final segment (0:30-0:43) features a scientific diagram displaying gene structures of various animal viruses—EIAV (horse), FIV/BIV/OMVV (cat, cow, sheep)—and HIV-1, showing genes like 'gag', 'pol', 'tat', and 'env'. Below these diagrams, a photograph shows a person wearing a dark shirt and a black headset or blindfold, getting blood drawn from their arm by another person, with medical supplies on a table. To the right of this photo is a detailed diagram of an HIV virus particle, illustrating its internal and external components.

The video segment opens with a complex image illustrating the genetic structures of various lentiviruses, including EIAV (equine infectious anemia virus), FIV/BIV/OMVV (feline immunodeficiency virus/bovine immunodeficiency virus/ovine maedi-visna virus), and HIV-1 (human immunodeficiency virus type 1), positioned next to corresponding animal hosts (horse, cat, cow, sheep). Below this, a person with dark hair and a beard, wearing a dark t-shirt, is seated at a table, appearing to interact with another person's extended arm, possibly for a medical procedure, with medical supplies visible. A detailed diagram of the HIV virus particle, showcasing its internal and external components, is also visible. The scene then transitions to a world map displaying pie charts that indicate the global distribution of different HIV subtypes (A, B, C, D, CRF_AE, Others), with a "Global Total" chart showing percentages. Below this map, a text overlay states, "Group M, Subtype B dominates the "West", Subtype C dominates Africa and Asia, and A dominates Central Europe and Russia." A phylogenetic tree diagram titled "HIV-1 HIV-2" is also shown, illustrating the hierarchical classification of HIV-1 groups and subtypes, with Group M and Subtype B highlighted in red boxes. The video concludes with a full-screen world map colored to show the "Adult prevalence rate" of an implied disease (HIV), ranging from light yellow for "< 0.1%" to dark red for "15.0 - 34.0%". Southern Africa is notably depicted in the darkest red, indicating the highest prevalence, while other regions like Russia and parts of Southeast Asia also show significant rates, contrasting with lighter-colored regions such as North America, South America, and Western Europe.

The video segment transitions through several still images, each illustrating a point in the accompanying audio. It begins with a digitally colored microscopic image (0:00-0:06) showing numerous small, bright red spherical objects (likely representing viruses) scattered across and interacting with larger, textured blue cellular structures, some of which appear to be budding or protruding. This is followed by a black and white transmission electron micrograph (0:06-0:14) depicting a cell membrane with dark, circular structures along its edge. Black arrows point to several of these structures, and white arrowheads point to others, indicating the process of budding. Below this image, white text on a black background reads: "Immunogold labeling of HIV virions budding from a cell membrane. Source: Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center," identifying the structures as HIV virions. The third image (0:14-0:26) displays a screenshot of a website with a large blue "WHALE" logo at the top and multiple columns of hyperlinked text on a white background, listing various categories such as "Medical Politics," "Big Brother," "Conspiracies," and "Mind Control." An overlaying black text box to the right of the website content states: "This entire website is one giant steaming pile of ... pseudoscience." The final image (0:26-0:27) is a plain white screen with black text centered, which reads: "C0nc0rdance's Rule:".

The video opens with black text "C0nc0rdance's Rule:" above blue text ""Never take medical advice from the Internet"" displayed on a white background. This is followed by a smiling man in a white doctor's coat and stethoscope, who is identified by accompanying black text as "Don't ask this guy, he's just a model for a stock photo." The text then disappears, leaving the doctor still smiling. The screen then splits to show two different smiling individuals, both appearing to be doctors: a woman in a white coat holding a stethoscope towards the viewer on the left, and a man in a white coat and glasses on the right. The scene transitions back to the initial white background with the rule, now slightly rephrased as "C0nc0rdance's Rule:" and ""Don't take medical advice from the Internet"". Finally, the screen turns black, displaying a 3D model of a DNA double helix, over which the yellow text "c0nc0rdance" fades in, and the DNA model fades out, leaving only the yellow text on a black background.
